the beta distribution is the unique fixed point of the random equation with a linear function, and that the beta distribution with the same parameters as the fixed point is also a stationary distribution for the Markov chain generated by the same linear function.

the beta distribution of a random variable is the unique solution of the following random equation: $$\beta = \alpha + \frac{\beta^{\beta-1}}{\alpha^{1-\beta}}\xi,$$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are parameters and $\xi$ is a random variable with the standard normal distribution.

the fixed point and the random solution of the random equation with a beta distributed solution are beta distributed, and that the random processes we study have limiting distributions that are also beta distributed.

we have found a new approach to solving a random equation with a beta distributed solution that also provides a solution to a related random equation, which in turn allows us to find the limiting distributions of the processes we consider.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta distribution is an important distributional limit for many different random processes.
beta distributed fixed points of linear random functions generate nested interval schemes that are useful for generating random variables and for solving stochastic optimization problems.
